chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created Adam from clay, so He prohibited eating clay upon his offspring.

key_terms.الطِّينِ: clay (the substance from which Adam was created)

ai.seo_question: Why is eating clay prohibited in Shia Islam according to the origin of Adam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a theological link between human origin and dietary law, asserting that the prohibition of eating clay is rooted in the fact that Adam was created from it. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted not merely as a physical restriction but as a sign of respect for the substance of one's creation, reinforcing the sanctity of the human form. The narration underscores the concept of 'fitrah' (innate nature), where physical origins inform spiritual and ethical conduct.
